description: P-51D-25-NA; Baugher 1944 file states on display at Volk Field ANGB Camp Douglas; serial lies inside the 44-72027/44-73028 P-51D-25-NA block; c/n from Aerial Visuals

F-86H-10-NH; USAF 3595th CCTW then Massachusetts ANG 101st TFS and New York ANG 138th TFS; written off 2 Sep 1965 then placed on display at Volk Field; serial inside the 53-1298/53-1528 F-86H-10-NH block
Built by General Motors Fisher Body as F-84F-25-GK; served 12th SFW 31st SFW Georgia ANG 128th FS Virginia ANG 149th FS then 366th TFW; Baugher records it preserved at Wisconsin ANG Camp Douglas
F-102A-70-CO; USAF 31st FIS and 317th FIS then Wisconsin ANG 176th FIS from 1975; Baugher and Aerial Visuals both place it at Volk Field

TF-102A-41-CO two-seat combat trainer; long USAF and ANG career ending with Wisconsin ANG 176th FIS; Baugher states currently preserved at the Volk Field ANG Museum; the museum's own page lists only F-102A so this second Deuce is easy to miss
F-100C-25-NA; Baugher entry reads simply on display at Volk Field ANGB Wisconsin
F-105B-20-RE; USAF 4th TFW then New Jersey ANG 119th TFS then USAFR 466th TFS; Baugher confirms display at Volk Field ANGB Camp Douglas

Modified to EF-4C Wild Weasel; 497th TFS 559th TFS 17th TRS 81st TFS then Indiana ANG 163rd and 113th TFS; ground trainer at Volk Field from 11/1987; sent to Hardwood Range as a target 8/1994 but recovered and Baugher records it on display at the Wisconsin National Guard Museum in 2011; Aerial Visuals still lists it at the Hardwood range which is stale
A-7D-8-CV; Baugher 1970 file states put on display at Volk Field Wisconsin
Baugher 1977 file states on display at Volk Field ANGB Wisconsin; carries IN tailcode markings per Aerial Visuals
Active July 1995 with 122nd Fighter Squadron Louisiana ANG; Baugher states on display with Wisconsin ANG Camp Douglas; the museum's own web page calls this an F-15C which is wrong for this serial

Built as KC-97G and converted to KC-97L; Baugher 1952 file states put on display at Volk Field ANGB Camp Douglas; Aerial Visuals still calls it a KC-97G which is the as-built variant not the display configuration
Baugher 1966 file states preserved at Volk Field WI; some sources call it a UH-1H which is the common D-to-H upgrade
Baugher 1970 file states on display at Volk Field WI; Aerial Visuals records it as a YAH-1S development airframe
